先找出克拉維的方向：是三在前還是二在前。整首曲子的重音都會指向它。: First find the direction of the clave: three-two or two-three. Every accent in the piece points to it.
克拉維不是鼓的一部分，而是全團共用的參考座標。它是一個兩小節的節奏型，通常記成三: The clave is not part of the drums but a reference coordinate shared by the whole group. It is a two-bar rhythmic pattern, usually written as a three-plus-two or two-plus-three combination: one side has three strokes and the other two, alternating between the two bars. Once the band decides on three-two or two-three, every part's accents, the starting point of phrases and the placing of horn stabs have to follow that direction. The clave can actually be struck on wooden sticks; in a large orquesta it is often not struck at all, and the players internalise the cycle and align to it inside their own parts, but in smaller line-ups such as the conjunto the clave sticks are usually still played by a percussionist. So the clave is more a shared contract of time than an instrument.
克拉維就是一種打擊樂器，由一位樂手負責敲。: The clave is a percussion instrument played by one player.
克拉維是一個兩小節的節奏循環，全團共用。它可以用木棒敲出來；在大型 orques: The clave is a two-bar rhythmic cycle shared by the whole group. It can be struck on wooden sticks; in a large orquesta it is often not actually played but internalised as the shared reference of all the parts, while in smaller line-ups such as the conjunto it is usually still struck by a percussionist. Treat it as one drummer's component and you miss its function of organising the whole group.
克拉維的方向在傳統上全曲固定：一首曲子從頭到尾維持「三在前」或「二在前」，中途翻: The direction of the clave is traditionally fixed for the whole piece: a piece keeps three-two or two-three from beginning to end, and turning it over midway is held to break the principle of the clave. Once the direction is set, every part's accents and phrase starts follow it; a very few modern arrangements experiment with turning it between sections, but that is not the norm. Because the direction is fixed, salsa's drive comes not from shifting the weight but from the constantly changing counterpoint and stabs of the parts inside the same cycle.
克拉維（clave，木棒）或全團內化的克拉維感: Clave (wooden sticks), or a sense of clave internalised by the whole group

呼喊回應（soneo–coro）是薩爾薩聲部關係的核心。主唱（sonero）唱一: Call and response (soneo–coro) is the core of salsa's part relations. The lead singer (sonero) sings an improvised solo line and the chorus or the whole band answers with a fixed line, the two alternating. This structure lets the music go on for a long time inside the same cycle, and lets the singer adjust the length of the phrases to the mood in the room. The clave does not change, the underlayer does not change; what changes is the conversation on top.
和紹羅的差別在編制與場合，也在低音的位置。紹羅是室內的器樂合奏，以器樂為主、歌唱: The difference from choro is the line-up and the occasion, and also where the bass sits. Choro is a chamber instrumental ensemble, mainly instrumental with singing only occasional, the players seated around together, harmony founded on the cavaquinho and the six-string guitar with a seven-string guitar on the bass line; salsa is a dance line-up with a singer and horns, and the bass's tumbao and the piano's montuno push the steps with syncopation and anticipation so that the dancers can predict the next accent. One is for listening, the other for dancing.
小號、長號（管樂組）；大型薩爾薩樂團另可加薩克斯風: Trumpets and trombones (the horn group); a large salsa band may add saxophones

康渾托與薩爾薩樂團出現在舞廳、俱樂部、節慶、婚禮與社區聚會。它的核心場合是「跳舞: The conjunto and the salsa band appear in dance halls, clubs, festivals, weddings and community gatherings. The core occasion is dancing: the rhythm has to let the dancers predict the next accent, so the clave cycle cannot be changed casually. Concert and studio versions allow more complex arrangements and longer passages.
康渾托與薩爾薩樂團的編制可以差很多，但分工邏輯一致：一個低音聲部、一個和聲聲部、: Conjunto and salsa band line-ups can differ a great deal, but the logic of the division is the same: one bass part, one harmonic part, a set of percussion instruments (each covering a different rhythmic layer), plus horns and a singer. The earlier small line-ups (sexteto/septeto) used the tres and the guitar for harmony, with bongó, maracas and double bass; the sexteto had no trumpet, and the septeto added one. From the 1940s the conjunto replaced the tres with the piano and added conga, timbales and two or three trumpets. The salsa band is larger still, adding three or four horns and a full percussion set.
康渾托（conjunto）與薩爾薩樂團（salsa band）是加勒比地區與紐約: The conjunto and the salsa band are dance line-ups that grew out of the Caribbean and the Latin communities of New York: bass, piano or tres, a set of percussion instruments and horns, with every part sharing one two-bar rhythmic cycle. The problem they solve is clear: let a group of people play complex rhythmic layers at the same time without falling apart. The answer is not a conductor but the clave.
曲目上，薩爾薩涵蓋頌（son）、瓜關科（guaguancó）、恰恰恰（chach: In repertoire salsa covers different rhythmic types — son, guaguancó, chachachá — each matching different steps and tempos; the montuno is a repeating passage inside a piece, not a rhythmic type alongside them. What they share is a cyclical structure organised by the clave: the same harmonic and rhythmic vocabulary can be played at different tempos and in different line-ups.
最容易被混為一談的是巴西的森巴打擊樂隊。兩者都以反覆的節奏循環與分層的打擊樂為核: The one most easily confused with it is the Brazilian samba bateria. Both build on repeating rhythmic cycles and layered percussion, but the reference for time is different: salsa's shared reference is the clave, a two-bar three-plus-two or two-plus-three cycle; the samba bateria's skeleton is the front-and-back pulse carried by the surdo drums divided among parts, with the cycle counted in two beats. The clave decides where the accents fall, the surdo decides where the body's weight falls.
標記段落、加 fill、以鼓邊與牛鈴（cencerro）製造提示: Marks sections, adds fills, and signals with rim shots and the cowbell (cencerro)
每個聲部都對齊克拉維，但不是每個聲部都演奏克拉維的節奏。低音、鋼琴、康加鼓各有自: Every part aligns to the clave, but not every part plays the clave's rhythm. The bass, the piano and the conga each have their own patterns, and it is these patterns interlocking inside the same cycle that make the salsa sound; everyone playing the same rhythm would lose the layers.

維持連續的細分聲響，填滿高頻；沙鈴是早期 sexteto／septeto 的標準: Keeps a continuous subdivided sound filling the high frequencies; the maracas were the standard percussion of the early sexteto/septeto, are occasionally seen but are not standard in the conjunto and salsa band, and the güiro is more often found in line-ups built on flute and violins such as the charanga
編制的差異也影響聲音。傳統康渾托較小、較乾，打擊樂器與撥弦樂器的聲音比較突出，適: The difference in line-up affects the sound too. The traditional conjunto is smaller and drier, the percussion and plucked strings more forward, suited to rooms and small venues. The salsa band is larger and thicker, piano and horns plus a full percussion set, suited to dance halls and large venues. They share the same rhythmic vocabulary, but the volume, the timbre and the occasions differ.
聽主唱與銅管的交替：誰唱、誰回應、什麼時候全團一起。: Listen to the alternation between the singer and the horns: who sings, who answers, when the whole band comes in together.
聽低音如何以切分與預期推動樂句。這是 tumbao 型最明顯的特徵。: Listen to how the bass pushes the phrases with syncopation and anticipation. This is the most obvious feature of the tumbao.
聽康加鼓與邦哥鼓的分工：一個較低、一個較高，兩者不是同一個節奏的重複。: Listen to the division between the conga and the bongó: one lower, one higher, and they are not the same rhythm repeated.
與馬拉卡圖的差別在誰下指令。馬拉卡圖的段落轉換由領唱歌手（cantor）的呼喊啟: The difference from maracatu is who gives the instructions. In maracatu the change of section is started by the call of the lead singer (cantor), a call and response; in salsa the change of section is often started by the timbales, the piano or a shout from the singer, while the direction of the clave stays fixed for the whole piece. One relies on a vocal signal, the other on cues inside the percussion layer.

薩爾薩是紐約與加勒比社群在二十世紀中後期形成的都市舞曲場景，它吸收了頌、蒙圖諾、: Salsa is an urban dance scene that took shape among New York and Caribbean communities in the middle and late twentieth century; it absorbed the rhythmic vocabulary of the son, the montuno and the guaguancó from Cuba and Puerto Rico, and with horns, piano and amplification formed a larger, thicker line-up. The name and the scene are different, but the music has many sources.
薩爾薩的每一個聲部都在演奏克拉維。: Every part in salsa plays the clave.
還有一個常被忽略的層次：薩爾薩的鋼琴蒙圖諾與低音 tumbao 並不是各自獨立的: There is one more layer that is often overlooked: the piano's montuno and the bass's tumbao are not independent of each other. The piano's chord pattern refers to where the bass accents fall, and the bass accents refer to the clave; the three make a chain of dependence. If any one part changes its pattern, the other two have to adjust, or the whole thing stops locking together. This is why salsa players spend so much rehearsal time aligning a few key beats rather than running the whole score from beginning to end. What they practise is the same spot on the same map, not the same version of the same passage.
銅管的角色和銅管組條目裡的邏輯相似：不負責時間，而是在時間上放置重音。薩爾薩樂團: The role of the horns follows the logic of the horn section entry: not responsible for time, but placing accents on it. A salsa band's horns often play unison passages (the mambo), which are written and repeatable and contrast with the singer's call and response. The call and response happens between the singer and the chorus: the singer sings a line and the chorus answers; the horns play background riffs over the montuno and sometimes take the coro line themselves; in the mambo the horns in unison become the main event, but the vocal soneo–coro dialogue usually carries on, the two overlapping in most arrangements rather than strictly alternating.
鋼琴的蒙圖諾與低音的 tumbao 是這份契約的具體實現。低音以根音與五度的交替: The piano's montuno and the bass's tumbao are the concrete form of that contract. The bass is built on alternating root and fifth, often pushing the root ahead of the next bar's downbeat and filling the gaps with passing notes, which makes it sound as if it is pushing rather than stepping. The piano's montuno is a fixed chord pattern played over and over, and sounds like a rhythm instrument that carries harmony. Together they make a continuous, directed underlayer, and that underlayer is not a chord progression but a groove that can repeat indefinitely. The singer and the horns come and go freely on top of it, because the underlayer does not change as they come and go.
鋼琴蒙圖諾（montuno）：固定的和弦型反覆，與低音咬合: Piano montuno: a fixed chord pattern repeated, interlocking with the bass
